content:
A number is decreased by 30%, then increased by 30% — and half of every class answers "no change". That one reflex, more than anything, is what the IMO Percentages questions are designed to catch. Scroll down for the free IMO Class 7 Percentages online test. Ten Olympiad-pattern MCQs, instant scoring. Under every question sits an explanation you can learn from.

What the IMO asks from Percentages in Class 7

  • Conversions between fractions, decimals and per cent.
  • Finding x% of a quantity; expressing one number as % of another.
  • Percentage increase and decrease.
  • Successive changes (the 30%-down-30%-up trap).
  • Word problems: marks, population, discounts.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • Successive changes MULTIPLY: −30% then +30% is 0.7 × 1.3 = 0.91 — a 9% decrease.
  • 5 : 8 as a percentage is 5/8 × 100 = 62.5%.
  • 0.00875 = 0.875% — moving to per cent multiplies by 100.
  • To undo a 20% increase you decrease by 16⅔%, not 20%.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Adding successive percentage changes.
  • Taking the percentage of the wrong base (new vs original).
  • Confusing percentage POINTS with percentage change.

questions.explanation: Multiplier = 1.20 × 0.80 = 0.96. Equal up-down changes of x% always lose (x²/100)% = 4%.

questions.explanation: Acid is unchanged: 0.3X = 0.2(X + 20). 0.1X = 4 gives X = 40 litres.
